definition: The study of carbon-containing compounds, especially those found in living organisms and derived from crude oil.
clues: This is a branch of chemistry
It focuses on a specific element's compounds
Carbon is central to this branch
The study of carbon-based compounds — including hydrocarbons, alcohols, carboxylic acids and polymers

definition: A compound containing only hydrogen and carbon atoms.
clues: This is a type of organic compound
It contains only two types of atom
Methane and ethane are examples
A compound made only of carbon and hydrogen — includes alkanes, alkenes and many fuels

definition: A mixture of hydrocarbons formed from the remains of ancient marine organisms over millions of years. A non-renewable fossil fuel.
clues: This is a natural resource found underground
It is a non-renewable fossil fuel
It is a mixture of different hydrocarbons
A complex mixture of hydrocarbons formed from ancient marine organisms — refined by fractional distillation to make fuels and chemicals

definition: The process used to separate crude oil into fractions based on differences in boiling point. Carried out in a fractionating column.
clues: This is a separation technique
It separates crude oil into useful components
It exploits differences in boiling points
Crude oil is heated and vapours condense at different levels of a column — separating it into fractions of different boiling points

definition: A mixture of hydrocarbons with similar boiling points obtained from fractional distillation of crude oil.
clues: This is a product of fractional distillation
It is a group of hydrocarbons with similar boiling points
Petrol, diesel and kerosene are examples
A collection of hydrocarbons with similar chain lengths and boiling points — separated from crude oil in a fractionating column

definition: A saturated hydrocarbon with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Contains only single C–C bonds. Examples: methane, ethane, propane, butane.
clues: This is a type of hydrocarbon
It contains only single carbon-carbon bonds
Its general formula is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂
A saturated hydrocarbon with only single C–C bonds — methane (CH₄), ethane (C₂H₆) and propane (C₃H₈) are examples

definition: A hydrocarbon that contains only single C–C bonds. Alkanes are saturated.
clues: This describes a type of hydrocarbon
It has only single carbon-carbon bonds
Alkanes are this type
A hydrocarbon with no double bonds between carbon atoms — all bonds are single C–C bonds, so no more hydrogen can be added

definition: An unsaturated hydrocarbon containing at least one C=C double bond. General formula: CₙH₂ₙ. Examples: ethene, propene.
clues: This is a type of hydrocarbon
It contains a carbon-carbon double bond
Its general formula is CₙH₂ₙ
An unsaturated hydrocarbon with at least one C=C double bond — ethene (C₂H₄) and propene (C₃H₆) are examples

definition: A hydrocarbon that contains one or more C=C double bonds. Alkenes are unsaturated.
clues: This describes a type of hydrocarbon
It contains at least one double bond
Alkenes are this type
A hydrocarbon containing a C=C double bond — it can undergo addition reactions because the double bond can open

definition: A test used to distinguish between alkanes and alkenes. Alkenes decolourise bromine water (orange to colourless); alkanes do not.
clues: This is a chemical test used to identify a type of hydrocarbon
Bromine water is used as the reagent
Alkenes decolourise the solution
Adding orange bromine water — it turns colourless with an alkene (due to addition reaction) but stays orange with an alkane

definition: A reaction in which two molecules react together to form a single product. Alkenes undergo addition reactions because of their C=C double bond.
clues: This is a type of chemical reaction
It produces a single product from two molecules
Alkenes undergo this type of reaction
Two molecules join together to make one product — alkenes react this way because the C=C double bond opens to accept new atoms

definition: The thermal decomposition of long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful ones. Produces alkanes and alkenes.
clues: This is a process used in the oil industry
It breaks down long hydrocarbon chains
It produces alkenes as one of the products
Heating long-chain alkanes with a catalyst breaks them into shorter, more useful molecules — including alkenes used to make polymers

definition: Cracking carried out using a zeolite (aluminium silicate) catalyst at moderate temperatures (~450°C). Produces branched alkanes and aromatic compounds.
clues: This is a type of cracking
It uses a catalyst
It operates at a lower temperature than thermal cracking
Long-chain hydrocarbons are broken over a zeolite catalyst at ~450°C — produces branched alkanes and aromatic compounds

definition: Cracking carried out at very high temperatures (up to 1000°C) and high pressures. Produces mainly alkenes.
clues: This is a type of cracking
It uses very high temperatures
It produces mainly alkenes
High temperature and pressure break long hydrocarbon chains — mainly producing alkenes used in polymer production

definition: The burning of a hydrocarbon with excess oxygen, producing only carbon dioxide and water.
clues: This is a type of combustion reaction
It requires excess oxygen
It only produces carbon dioxide and water
Burning a fuel with plenty of oxygen — only CO₂ and H₂O are produced; no carbon monoxide or soot

definition: The burning of a hydrocarbon with insufficient oxygen, producing carbon monoxide, soot (carbon) and water.
clues: This is a type of combustion reaction
It occurs when oxygen is limited
It produces toxic carbon monoxide
Burning a fuel in limited oxygen — produces CO (toxic), soot (C) and water instead of just CO₂ and H₂O

definition: An organic compound containing the –OH (hydroxyl) functional group. General formula: CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH. Examples: methanol, ethanol, propanol.
clues: This is a type of organic compound
It contains a hydroxyl functional group
Ethanol is the most well-known example
An organic compound with the –OH group — methanol, ethanol and propanol are examples, used as fuels and solvents

definition: The alcohol found in alcoholic drinks. Formula: C₂H₅OH. Can be produced by fermentation or by hydration of ethene.
clues: This is a specific type of alcohol
It is found in alcoholic drinks
Its formula is C₂H₅OH
The alcohol in beer, wine and spirits — produced by fermentation of sugars or by the hydration of ethene

definition: The anaerobic process by which yeast converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide.
clues: This is a biological process used to make alcohol
It is carried out by yeast
Glucose is converted into ethanol and CO₂
Yeast anaerobically respires glucose to produce ethanol and carbon dioxide — used to make beer, wine and biofuels

definition: An organic compound containing the –COOH functional group. Examples: methanoic acid, ethanoic acid (vinegar). Weak acids.
clues: This is a type of organic compound
It contains the –COOH functional group
Ethanoic acid (vinegar) is an example
An organic compound with the carboxyl group –COOH — they are weak acids; ethanoic acid is found in vinegar

definition: An organic compound formed by the reaction between a carboxylic acid and an alcohol. Esters are used as flavourings and perfumes.
clues: This is a type of organic compound
It is formed from a carboxylic acid and an alcohol
It has a sweet, fruity smell
Formed by reacting a carboxylic acid with an alcohol (esterification) — used as flavourings, perfumes and solvents

definition: A polymer formed by the joining of many alkene monomers through opening of their C=C double bonds. No other products are formed.
clues: This is a type of polymer
It is formed from alkene monomers
No by-products are produced
Many alkene monomers open their double bonds and link together — the polymer is the only product formed

definition: A type of polymerisation where monomers join together with the loss of a small molecule (usually water) for each bond formed.
clues: This is a type of polymerisation
A small molecule is lost each time monomers join
Nylon and polyester are made this way
Monomers join with loss of water (or HCl) at each step — produces polymers like nylon and polyester

definition: A condensation polymer made from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid. Used in clothing, ropes and parachutes.
clues: This is a type of condensation polymer
It is used in fabrics and ropes
It is made from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid
A strong synthetic fibre made by condensation polymerisation — used in clothing, ropes and engineering materials

definition: A condensation polymer made from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid. Used in clothing and plastic bottles (PET).
clues: This is a type of condensation polymer
It is used in clothing and bottles
It is made from a diol and a dicarboxylic acid
A polymer made by condensation of a diol and a dicarboxylic acid — PET is used in plastic bottles and polyester fabric

definition: A naturally occurring condensation polymer made of nucleotide monomers. Stores genetic information in living organisms.
clues: This is a naturally occurring condensation polymer
Its monomers are nucleotides
It stores genetic information
A biological condensation polymer made of nucleotide monomers — it stores the genetic code in all living organisms

definition: The monomer unit of a protein. Contains both an amine (–NH₂) and a carboxylic acid (–COOH) group.
clues: This is the monomer of a protein
It contains two specific functional groups
It has both an amine group and a carboxyl group
The building block of proteins — contains –NH₂ and –COOH groups; amino acids join by condensation polymerisation to form proteins

definition: An atom or group of atoms in an organic molecule responsible for its characteristic chemical reactions.
clues: This is a term used in organic chemistry
It is the part of a molecule that determines its reactivity
–OH, –COOH and C=C are examples
The reactive part of an organic molecule — e.g. –OH in alcohols, –COOH in carboxylic acids, C=C in alkenes
